author: visegrad24
text:
The right-wing AfD party scored major gains in both of Sunday’s German elections, winning Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania with 38.2% of the vote while surging to a record 16.3% in Berlin.

In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the AfD more than doubled its 16.7% result from 2021 and overtook the governing SPD, which finished second with 35.5%.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s CDU suffered a historic collapse, receiving just 4.9% and failing to cross the 5% threshold. It will therefore have no seats in the state parliament, the first time the CDU has ever failed to enter a German state legislature.

The AfD also made major gains in Berlin despite finishing third.
It received 16.3% of the second vote, up from just 9.1% in the previous election, an increase of 7.2 percentage points and the party’s strongest result ever in the German capital.

The results came just two weeks after the AfD also finished first in Saxony-Anhalt, underscoring its rapidly expanding electoral strength in eastern Germany.
